title: Research: conditional blockwise P104 lifting at linear precision
body:
PR3033's exact P104 lifting split leaves `O(N r²)` narrow work at linear precision. This package constructs an exact blocked replacement and proves a **conditional addressed-array bound** `O(N[W r h^(-a)+r h])`, with every wide backend call, narrow pass, cube transfer and clean uncomputation charged. At `W=Theta(r)`, the conditional saving is `a/(1+a)`.

The backend premise is explicit: source-preserving exact oracles for both scaled ideal orientations with a uniform complete tariff and workspace. The direct Walsh reference supplies semantics, not this fast backend. Physical routing, clean/dirty stock admission, actual native recipes and the full supplier/outer comparison remain open. **No new kappa, admitted supplier, selected-record change or physical runtime gain is claimed.** This mechanism cannot bootstrap itself: `a/(1+a)<a`.

Only `research/p104-blockwise-lifting/` is added. The ordinary written proof includes the exact tail block, signed ranges, four backend calls per local cube including cleanup, paid global/local indexing, and an `O(N n)` affine/quadratic-Z4 wrapper compiler with charged control storage. Complete macro invoices and arbitrary dirty XOR targets are checked separately from Python allocation or physical tape behavior.

Validation: registered Python 3.12 replay passed; optimized Python 3.14 and Git-free read-only export controls passed. The two internal mathematical specialists independently checked the identity and full recurrence. Finite coverage includes all 127 consecutive compositions through rank seven, 31,046 exhaustive signed partition/direction cases, 4,096-bit fixtures, 3,830 exact cost cases and separate Gray compiler checks. Review caught and fixed an accepted-input signed-width bug and quadratic sorting overhead; their controls remain in the package. These are AI-assisted internal checks and an ordinary written conditional proof, not human or formal-kernel review. Hosted CI is separate; no rerun or workflow dispatch is requested.

Predecessor credit: Tekalign/PR3033 `b12bbaeb5ca2e83f15433fc2dd0ba3b766595281` for the split, sharp guard, Walsh reference and linear-precision handoff; PR3025 for the literal lifting word, with ywz65, Arham Tahir and the retained P104/native/compiler lineage. Exact source bytes/Git blobs are preserved. Prepared for Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-blockwise-lifting
```

[Canonical investigation and claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2750#discussioncomment-18983485). Base canonical main `d8e0f83f00191df62174b641e9fff055c357f641`, priority revision 6. Scope, stop gates and open next questions are in README/TASK; the next step is an actual exact backend and its complete physical/stock invoice.
